thread:
support_jess: FYI / escalated from support — AcmeCorp is seeing repeated 504s and timeouts from hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. They report long tail latencies, some requests stuck in queue. sample req ids: r_9a8b7c, r_f00ba7. customer on call now. :rotating_light:

sre_tom: pinging infra, can you paste a traceback or gateway logs?

support_jess: here's the gateway log excerpt they attached:

```
2026-03-17T09:12:05Z gateway host=gw-12 REQ=r_9a8b7c status=504 queue_depth=95 handler=dequeue duration_ms=120005
2026-03-17T09:12:06Z gateway host=gw-12 REQ=r_f00ba7 status=504 queue_depth=98 reason=tail_timeout
2026-03-17T09:12:07Z gateway host=gw-12 REQ=r_1c2d3e status=200 queue_depth=99
```

eng_batch: those queue_depth values are near our per-host soft limit (100). Looks like continuous-batcher backlog growth. Any tenant-specific spikes?

support_jess: AcmeCorp traffic looks normal per their dashboard — small spike but within contract. They said shift started when they enabled streaming option on many clients.

infra_ana: I'm pulling host metrics — batcher lag and kv-cache miss rate. Early findings: batcher backpressure started at 09:08 UTC, p95 dequeue went from 90ms -> 30s by 09:12. KV cache cold miss rate jumped. Possibly many unique prefixes from streaming requests preventing batching.

oncall: tagging runbook-queue-saturation. First action: identify offending tenant, consider soft-throttle and fallback model. Also check auth/billing anomalies because we saw a billing-job spike last week.

billing-bot: Alert: spike in billing API calls for AcmeCorp at 09:05 UTC — 4x baseline. No rate-limit hits recorded.

eng_batch: Could be clients hitting with unique streaming session ids preventing request coalescing — continuous batching performance degrades when sequence lengths vary widely. Suggest forcing per-tenant batching mode to 'passthrough' temporarily.

sre_tom: Can we repro locally? Steps requested: 1) start batcher with continuous batching enabled 2) send many small streaming requests with unique prefixes 3) observe queue depth and p95 dequeue. Anyone on infra can try repro on canary?

infra_ana: Spawning a canary pod now in eu-west-1 with identical config to hosted pool. Running replay with 500 reqs/min with unique prefixes. Attaching probe: `curl -sS $CANARY/gateway/metrics | grep queue_depth`.

opsbot: Deploy started: canary-hosted-queue-repro -> pod/canary-queue-01 ; logs forwarding to #incidents for 15m.

eng_batch: Local repro shows continuous-batcher queues up and KV cache is leaking entries because streaming prefixes never reused. p95 dequeue climbs to 45s with queue_depth ~105. Code note: our eviction policy uses LRU with window of 10k keys; streaming sessions blow past that.

support_jess: Customer on call says timeouts are user-facing on their product search API, they need a mitigation ASAP.

sre_tom: Short-term mitigations: 1) enable tenant-specific throttle to cap inflight requests to 50 2) enable fallback to smaller non-streaming model variant for this tenant 3) increase per-host soft queue limit from 100 -> 150 as emergency. Which one can we do without infra deploy?

infra_ana: We can change soft-limit and tenant throttle via feature flags in control plane (no infra deploy). I'll raise soft_limit to 150 for the affected pool and enable throttle for AcmeCorp. Applying now.

opsbot: Feature flag update applied: `queue.soft_limit=150` to pool-hosted-eu-west. Tenant throttle `acmecorp.max_inflight=50` enabled.

eng_batch: Also toggled continuous-batching for that tenant to 'disabled' via config — this forces passthrough. If they were using streaming, fallbacks may change behavior.

support_jess: Pushed changes. Customer reports requests returning again but some rate-limited errors (429) at first. They confirm success rates improving to ~95% within 3 minutes. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Note: enabling passthrough increases per-token cost — flagged for finance.

oncall: Good recovery. Next steps: 1) collect traces for the 09:00–09:20 window 2) run a more controlled load test to tune KV cache size and eviction policy 3) decide if we need a persistent change for streaming workloads (e.g., session-aware batching or better prefix canonicalization) 4) review customer-facing postmortem with AcmeCorp.

eng_batch: Paging a small follow-up: we should add a metric exposing per-tenant unique-prefix rate — that would have alerted earlier. Filing ticket: INF-6721.

sre_tom: For the postmortem, save these artifacts: gateway logs, batcher traces, kv-cache eviction logs, canary repro script. Also include the short-term config diffs (soft_limit change, tenant throttle, passthrough toggle).

support_jess: I'll coordinate the customer comms and schedule a follow-up call for 16:00 UTC.

infra_ana: Uploading canary logs to /tmp/incidents/1764503333-canary-logs.tar.gz and snapshotting metrics.

opsbot: Incident annotated: severity=high, status=mitigated, runbook=queue-saturation, incident_id=INC-2026-0421-9

sre_tom: Closing note: this looks like a pattern where streaming clients create many single-use prefixes which kill continuous-batching efficiency. Eng to propose long-term fixes: prefix canonicalization, session affinity, or batching heuristics.

support_jess: Customer happy with mitigation and asks for ETA on permanent fix. I'll loop back when we have a plan.

eng_batch: Will draft a proposal and timeline. Thanks everyone.
